all the three series of sulfonamides tested here are endowed with interesting inhibitory activity against hCAs I and II, but the best inhibitory activity was obtained with the sulfonamidic series 6a-f, which are characterized by a (4-oxo-thiazolidin-ylidene-aminoethyl)-indolin-2-one moiety.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have synthesized a series of novel sulfamides incorporating indolin-2-ones as tails and tested them as CAIs.

the indolin-2-ones-based sulfonamiders reported here are potent hCA I, hCA II and hCA IV inhibitors, and that the aminoethyl or (thiazolidine-2-yl)aminoethyl linker connecting the sulfonamide moiety to indolin-2-on moiety is crucial for their activity.

we have designed, synthesized and biologically evaluated three different series of sulfonamides, which incorporate indolin-2-ones (as tails) attached to the sulfonamide zinc anchoring moiety via different linkers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sulfonamides containing indolin-2-ones as tail groups are promising inhibitors of hCAs, especially for the hCA II isoform, and could represent a new class of CAIs.
the presence of an indolin-2-onesulfonamide scaffold is a good strategy to obtain novel, potent and selective inhibitors of hCAs.

the indolin-2-ones can act as a good tail for the synthesis of new sulfonamides endowed with good inhibitory activity against several hCA isoforms, thus opening up new venues in the field of sulfonamide-based inhibitors of this important class of metalloenzymes.
